candidats.description: Hibiya Public Hall [Shisei Kaikan], in part a public facility and in part the offices of the Tokyo Institute of Municipal Research, is located on the southeastern corner of Hibiya Park. The ten-story steel-frame reinforced concrete structure is finished in terra cotta, Yokonezawa stone (quarried in Shizuoka Prefecture), and the light brown scratch tile so popular in the 1920s. Construction was completed in 1929, a symbol of Tokyo’s rebirth after the devastating 1923 Great Kanto earthquake, and the hall is still in use today for concerts, lectures, meetings and other cultural activities. candidats.description: Earthquake damage caused to the Imperial County Services Building in the 1979 Imperial Valley earthquake . The support pillar failed at the east end of the Imperial County Services Building in El Centro . The concrete at the base of the columns was shattered and the vertical reinforced bars were severely bent, allowing the building to sag about 30 cm. This 6-story reinforced concrete frame and shear wall structure, designed to be earthquake resistant, was completed in 1971 at a construction cost of $1.87 million. candidats.description: Modern architecture in Holborn. Seen after we left the British Museum. Initially we were heading down New Oxford Street. I wasn't sure which way Tottenham Court Road Underground Station was, so ended up going via Centre Saint Giles onto High Holborn (then found our way to Holborn Underground Station). Was probably better to go there, as only had to get two tube trains back to Victoria. Centre Point seen down New Oxford Street. It's at 101–103 New Oxford Street. Built between 1961 and 1966.
